changes.what: Flattened transform arguments in every transform that had them (null_if, regex_extract, and the new length_in). They now sit at the top level of the transform object, e.g. {"op": "regex_extract", "pattern": ..., "group": 1}, instead of under an "args" key.
changes.why: The engine raised KeyError: 'pattern' on all 101 rows of legal_name, trading_name, address.state and address.postcode. The vocabulary shape is {"op": name, ...args}, so I had wrapped the arguments wrongly. The null_if on address.full did not error, but its args were nested too and may have been silently ignored, so I flattened it as well.

changes.what: Changed the ABN transforms to strip, digits_only, length_in [11], abn.
changes.why: The ABN error rate was 0.07, above the 0.05 limit. Some of the failures were not checksum failures at all. They were cells that cannot be a single ABN, such as the semicolon-joined multi-ABN cell (33 digits) and 12-digit values like '520 583 909 917'. These now route to 'no value' instead of a parse error, and they are still never emitted. Genuine 11-digit checksum failures (e.g. 86 087 097 717) are still rejected by the abn transform. I did not loosen the checksum, because emitting an invalid ABN is worse than dropping it. The remaining error rate is real source data-entry error.

changes.what: Updated the ABN rationale and notes to say that residual checksum failures are genuine source errors.
changes.why: Reviewers should know that any remaining ABN errors come from the data and are not a mapping bug.

changes.what: Checked the preview against meaning. No mappings were added or removed, and confidences are unchanged.
changes.why: The address.full values are supplier street addresses, and the ABNs shown are plausible. The preview rows for legal_name, trading_name, state and postcode all errored, so those values still need checking on the next run. Names like 'Kerr Australia' have no company suffix, so I kept legal_name at 0.7 and flagged it.

changes.what: Removed the entity.trading_name mapping and moved it to unmapped_canonical_fields.
changes.why: It had a 99% error rate because regex_extract with required:true raises an error on every row without '(Trading As ...)'. Only 1 of 101 rows produced a value. Setting required:false is not a safe fix, because I can't confirm what the engine emits on a non-match. If it passed the whole cell through, the legal name would be emitted as a trading name, which is worse than no mapping. Prefer unmapping over a fragile transform.

changes.what: Added a null_if for 'Refer to Queensland Government Arrangements Directory' to the start of the address.state and address.postcode chains.
changes.why: The placeholder rows were a direct source of errors (error rate 0.141, above the 0.05 limit). They are now treated as missing, as address.full already does.

changes.what: Set required:false on the regex_extract in address.state and address.postcode.
changes.why: Addresses with no state token or no trailing postcode, and multi-address cells, are expected and should give no value rather than a parse error. Examples are '805/220 Collins Street, Melbourne', '77-79 Ricketts Rd Mt Waverley', 'Bowen Hills 4006' and the ';'-separated cells. The regex stays anchored to 'STATE postcode' at the end, so it still never guesses. If a non-match fell through unchanged, the following state/postcode transform would reject it, so no wrong value could be emitted.
Recorded that trading_name is dropped, that '(Trading As X)' text is now stripped from legal_name and lost, and that the reviewer should confirm required:false gives no value on a non-match.
